title: Hardware Support
subtitle: Guess the hidden PC-hardware terms -- spin for consonants, buy vowels

gradeLabels.f: F-RANK -- Back to the Anti-Static Bag

puzzles.hint: A high-speed interface that runs at forty gigabits per second over a reversible USB-C port.
puzzles.explain: Thunderbolt 3 and 4 both operate at 40 Gbps over a USB-C connector and can carry data, video, and power on a single cable. It is backward-compatible with USB and DisplayPort devices.

puzzles.hint: A UEFI firmware setting that refuses to run operating system loaders that lack a valid cryptographic signature.
puzzles.explain: When enabled, the firmware checks each bootloader against a database of trusted signatures and blocks anything unsigned, preventing rootkits from loading before the OS. It is required for Windows 11 installation.

puzzles.hint: A configuration using two matched sticks seated in the correct paired slots to roughly double the data path to the processor.
puzzles.explain: Placing identical modules in slots A2 and B2 (the same-colored slots on most boards) activates this mode, which widens the effective memory bus and increases bandwidth for memory-intensive workloads.

puzzles.hint: A RAID technique that spreads redundancy information across every drive in the array so no single disk holds all recovery data.
puzzles.explain: RAID 5 writes parity blocks in rotation across all member drives, allowing the array to reconstruct data after any single drive fails. Usable capacity equals N minus one drives.

puzzles.hint: The component that converts the alternating current from a wall outlet into the regulated direct current voltages the motherboard and drives need.
puzzles.explain: It outputs three primary DC rails: plus twelve volt for motors and PCIe devices, plus five volt for legacy connectors, and plus three point three volt for modern logic circuits. The wattage rating indicates maximum total output.

puzzles.hint: A compound applied in a pea-size dot between a processor and its heatsink to fill microscopic surface imperfections and improve conduction.
puzzles.explain: Even polished metal surfaces have tiny air gaps at the microscopic level; this compound, typically silicone or liquid metal based, displaces those air pockets and dramatically lowers junction temperatures.

puzzles.hint: A replaceable consumable in a laser printer that holds fine charged powder fused onto paper by a heated element.
puzzles.explain: The OPC drum receives a latent image from the laser, then attracts the fine powder from this consumable to form the image before it is pressed onto paper and permanently fused by a roller heated to approximately two hundred degrees Celsius.

puzzles.hint: A small diagnostic adapter seated in an expansion slot that shows a two-digit hexadecimal readout indicating exactly where startup self-testing stalled.
puzzles.explain: During the power-on self-test sequence the firmware writes progress codes to a specific I/O port; this diagnostic adapter reads those codes and shows them on its onboard display, allowing a technician to identify failed components even when nothing appears on screen.
